final_answer: For channel=='main' / scope=='bridge' tasks ONLY, replace the character/regex-based Test-IsLargeTask (lib/prompt-builder.ps1:538-551) with a multi-signal scope classifier driven by acceptance_count, subsystem_count, and intent.estimated_turns, preserving the existing atom/decomposed-child early-return so already-split work never re-classifies as large. When a task scores large, the planner is contractually required to emit a [[PROJECT_BACKLOG]] JSON split plus [[DECOMPOSED:N]] markers, ingested through the EXISTING Add-ProjectBacklogFromMarker(Channel='main') path (lib/backlog-autopilot.ps1:1383) as the single ingest path — no new parallel plumbing. A 'valid split' is defined deterministically from that ingest's return object (created>=2, errors empty, and every created atom is single-file with concrete acceptance/checks and parent linkage via source_task_id), not by re-scanning tags. Decomposition is MANDATORY: if a large bridge-self parent lacks a valid split, the driver blocks STATUS: CONTINUE to the coder and forces a bounded decompose-retry (2-3 attempts) that feeds the deterministic ingest errors back into the retry prompt; on exhaustion the parent transitions to operator-hold and NEVER falls back to coding the monolith. Children of the already-approved parent are created with status 'approved' (superseding the current Add-Idea status='new' path at lib/backlog-crud.ps1:74-89), tagged as bridge-self atoms, and linked to the parent, so they bypass ONLY the per-decomposition re-approval — not all control-plane safety. The whole mechanism is fenced to main/bridge; PROJECT channels keep Start-ProjectAutopilotIfNeeded (lib/backlog-autopilot.ps1:977) and F1-F4 operator approval untouched, guarded by mandatory regression tests. We REJECT a standing mandatory operator-review gate (atom_10): it contradicts the consensus 'no new gates' principle (atom_08) and the automated-child mechanism (atom_04), and defeats the bridge-self autopilot's purpose. Its legitimate oversight intent is preserved more cheaply by the operator-hold on retry exhaustion (atom_07) plus PROJECT-channel regression coverage (atom_11). This is design-only: the deliverable is this MAP/PLAN plus the atom list for operator review before implementation.

decisions.decision: atom_01 — Replace Test-IsLargeTask with a SCOPE profile: large := f(acceptance_count, subsystem_count, intent.estimated_turns), keeping the `Tags -contains 'atom'/'decomposed-child'` early-return.
decisions.rationale: Full A/B/C consensus, judge total 0.8125. The current heuristic (lib/prompt-builder.ps1:542-549) measures words/regex-file-mentions, so a short-but-wide order ('build service X') is huge in meaning yet tiny in text and slips through. A multi-signal scope classifier is a sounder, testable classifier; the early-return preserves idempotency so split atoms never re-trip the gate.
alternatives_considered: Keep char-length + regex-file heuristic (rejected: misses short-but-wide scope, the root cause of commit_famine)
Single-signal estimated_turns only (weaker: misses wide-acceptance tasks with low turn estimates)
decisions.risk: Threshold mis-calibration (false positives force needless decomposition; false negatives leak monoliths to the coder). estimated_turns may be absent on some intents.
decisions.test: Test-IsLargeTask returns true for a short-text/high-acceptance idea ('Build service X' impacting multiple subsystems / 10 acceptance criteria) and false for an atom/decomposed-child-tagged task.

decisions.decision: atom_05 — Fence the ENTIRE mechanism to channel=='main' / scope=='bridge'. PROJECT channels keep Start-ProjectAutopilotIfNeeded and F1-F4 approval unchanged.
decisions.rationale: Consensus and the highest-scoring atom (0.8875). This is the blast-radius control that makes every other atom safe to ship: PROJECT plans still flow through F1-F4 operator approval, satisfying the anti-Frankenstein constraint. Low cost, high reversibility, directly testable.
alternatives_considered: Apply decomposition to all channels (rejected: violates anti-Frankenstein gate and the contract's hard constraint)
Per-task opt-in flag instead of channel fence (rejected: weaker invariant, more surface area)
decisions.risk: A future channel-routing refactor could leak the path to PROJECT channels if the fence is checked in only one place.
decisions.test: Submit a large PROJECT-channel task: it still requires F1-F4 operator approval and does NOT auto-split; Start-ProjectAutopilotIfNeeded still returns not-project-channel behavior for main.

decisions.decision: atom_08 — Consolidate to ONE largeness function, ONE ingest path, ONE gate site; reuse the existing [[DECOMPOSED]] handler; deprecate/redirect the Add-Idea(status='new') child path; add NO new goals.md or parallel approval gates.
decisions.rationale: Consensus (A/B), judge 0.8775, maximal simplicity. This is the governing architectural principle and the explicit basis for rejecting atom_10. Satisfies the contract constraints to reuse existing plumbing and not multiply conflicting gates.
alternatives_considered: A new dedicated bridge-self decomposition subsystem (rejected: duplicates atom-ingest plumbing, contradicts the reuse constraint)
A new goals.md policy gate (rejected: multiplies conflicting gates)
decisions.risk: Redirecting the Add-Idea(status='new') child path (lib/backlog-crud.ps1:74-89) could affect non-decomposition callers if not carefully scoped to the bridge-self atom case.
decisions.test: Static audit confirms exactly one largeness function, one ingest path (Add-ProjectBacklogFromMarker), one gate site, and zero new policy docs/approval gates.

decisions.decision: atom_09 — The planner, for a large bridge-self parent, must emit BOTH a [[PROJECT_BACKLOG]] JSON block (with required per-atom metadata: single target file, acceptance/checks, parent linkage) AND [[DECOMPOSED:N]] markers.
decisions.rationale: From A only (0.7675) but it specifies the planner contract that atom_02 and atom_06 depend on, and is consistent with reusing the [[DECOMPOSED]] handler (atom_08). Without a precise output contract the ingest path has nothing deterministic to validate.
alternatives_considered: Emit only [[PROJECT_BACKLOG]] JSON and derive N from it (simpler; deferred as an open question to avoid redundancy)
Free-form planner output parsed heuristically (rejected: non-deterministic, the failure mode we are removing)
decisions.risk: Mild redundancy — N is derivable from the JSON length, so the dual marker can drift out of sync; treat the JSON as source of truth.
decisions.test: The planner prompt for a large main task instructs and produces [[PROJECT_BACKLOG]] JSON with the required schema plus [[DECOMPOSED:N]] markers.

decisions.decision: atom_02 — Route bridge-self decomposition through the EXISTING Add-ProjectBacklogFromMarker(Channel='main') as the single atom-ingest path, emitting [[PROJECT_BACKLOG]] JSON instead of raw Add-Idea.
decisions.rationale: Consensus (0.84), high specificity. Reuses proven plumbing (lib/backlog-autopilot.ps1:1383, where isBridgeSelfBacklog is already computed for Channel=='main') and directly enables atom_08's consolidation. Low integration risk.
alternatives_considered: A new bridge-self ingest function (rejected: parallel path, violates reuse constraint)
Direct Add-Idea calls per atom (rejected: bypasses dedup/slug/return-contract machinery atom_06 relies on)
decisions.risk: Add-ProjectBacklogFromMarker behavior is currently tuned for project backlogs; bridge-self atom semantics (approved children, bridge-self tag) must be threaded without disturbing project callers.
decisions.test: For a large main task, Add-ProjectBacklogFromMarker is invoked with Channel='main' and a [[PROJECT_BACKLOG]] JSON block, returning a {created, skipped, errors, ids} object.

decisions.decision: atom_06 — Define 'valid split' DETERMINISTICALLY from the ingest return value: created>=2, errors empty, and each created atom has exactly one target file, concrete acceptance/checks, and parent linkage — not by re-scanning tags.
decisions.rationale: Strong consensus (A/B), judge 0.825, highest specificity (0.95). Removes a fragile, race-prone tag re-scan and gives atom_03 a precise, machine-checkable gate condition. The ingest already returns created/skipped/errors/ids (confirmed at lib/backlog-autopilot.ps1:1386), so the signal exists.
alternatives_considered: Re-scan backlog for [[DECOMPOSED]]/atom tags after ingest (rejected: race-prone, non-deterministic)
Trust planner self-report of split validity (rejected: the planner is the component that fails)
decisions.risk: Requires the ingest to surface per-atom validation (single-file, acceptance present) in its return; if it only reports counts, additional per-atom checks must be added.
decisions.test: Parent closes/advances only when ingest reports >=2 single-file approved atoms with acceptance/checks and parent linkage; otherwise the split is judged invalid.

decisions.decision: atom_04 (MODIFIED per judge) — Children of an APPROVED decomposed parent are created with status 'approved', tagged as bridge-self atoms, and linked to the parent via source_task_id. They bypass ONLY the per-decomposition re-approval — NOT all control-plane safety. Human oversight is preserved via the parent's prior approval and atom_07's operator-hold on retry exhaustion.
decisions.rationale: Consensus on the mechanism (0.7725 after a 0.03 penalty). Resolves the atom_04/atom_10 conflict in favor of automation, consistent with atom_08's 'no new gates'. The judge's required wording change: do not claim children 'bypass approval/control-plane gates' wholesale — they bypass only the redundant re-approval of work whose parent an operator already approved.
alternatives_considered: Children created 'new' (current behavior, lib/backlog-crud.ps1:74-89) (rejected: re-sticks on approval + control-plane gates, the documented failure)
Children created 'pending-operator-review' (atom_10's variant) (rejected: re-introduces human latency, contradicts atom_08)
decisions.risk: Auto-approving children widens the automated path; a flawed split could push wrong atoms toward the coder. Mitigated by atom_06's valid-split definition, atom_03's mandatory gate, and atom_07's operator-hold.
decisions.test: Children are created status='approved', tagged bridge-self, linked to the parent via source_task_id, and proceed through the coder pipeline without re-sticking on approval/control-plane gates; tracked atoms commit in < 15 minutes.

decisions.decision: atom_03 — Decomposition is MANDATORY: when a large bridge-self parent lacks a valid split (per atom_06), the driver blocks STATUS: CONTINUE to the coder and forces a decompose-retry.
decisions.rationale: Consensus (0.81), risk_reduction 0.9. This is the core safety invariant that prevents handing the coder a monolith — the direct fix for the commit_famine / 45-minute output-cap kills. Upgrades [[DECOMPOSED]] from a request to an enforced gate. Depends on atom_06 (split definition) and atom_07 (retry/hold).
alternatives_considered: Keep [[DECOMPOSED]] as advisory request only (rejected: current behavior merely ASKS and the planner ships monoliths anyway)
Hard-fail the parent immediately with no retry (rejected: wastes a recoverable planner miss; atom_07 retry is cheaper)
decisions.risk: Low reversibility and added control-flow complexity; a bug here could deadlock a large task. Bounded by atom_07's retry cap and operator-hold terminal state.
decisions.test: A large main task with no valid split does NOT dispatch the coder; after the retry cap it is held for operator review.

decisions.decision: atom_07 — Implement bounded decompose-retry (2-3 attempts) that feeds the deterministic ingest errors back into the retry prompt, then transition to operator-hold; never fall back to coding the monolith.
decisions.rationale: From B only (0.795) but completes atom_03 and is the reconciliation point for the atom_04/atom_10 conflict — the single human touchpoint lives HERE (hold on exhaustion), not in a per-decomposition gate. Feeding atom_06's concrete errors back makes retries informative rather than blind.
alternatives_considered: Unbounded retry (rejected: can loop forever on an undecomposable task)
Immediate operator-hold with no retry (rejected: gives up on recoverable planner misses)
Fall back to coding the monolith after N tries (rejected: reintroduces the exact failure being fixed)
decisions.risk: Operator-hold requires a surfacing/notification mechanism; if none exists, held parents could be silently stuck.
decisions.test: Decompose-retry is capped (e.g., 3 attempts); on exhaustion the parent is set to 'held' for operator review and the coder is never dispatched the monolith.

decisions.decision: atom_11 — Add mandatory regression tests proving PROJECT-channel non-interference and unchanged F1-F4 behavior.
decisions.rationale: From A only (0.825), the verification counterpart to atom_05. Converts the isolation guarantee into a continuously checked invariant and partially substitutes for atom_10's oversight concern. Purely additive, low cost, high risk-reduction.
alternatives_considered: Rely on manual spot-checks of PROJECT channels (rejected: not durable, the isolation invariant is critical)
No dedicated tests, trust the channel fence (rejected: fence regressions would go undetected)
decisions.risk: Test specificity — must name the exact channels/cases (Start-ProjectAutopilotIfNeeded not-project-channel for main, F1-F4 still required, no auto-split on PROJECT) or coverage gaps remain.
decisions.test: New regression tests cover PROJECT-channel non-interference and unchanged F1-F4 behavior, and a large PROJECT task still requires operator approval with no auto-split.

rejected.decision: atom_10 — Mandatory operator review of the MAP/PLAN and the atom list as a standing gate BEFORE auto-approval and coder dispatch.
rejected.why: From C only, judge total 0.5725 (correctness 0.45, simplicity 0.40), flagged blocking. It introduces a NEW standing approval gate, directly contradicting consensus atom_08 ('no new parallel approval gates') and consensus atom_04 (children created approved), and it defeats the bridge-self autopilot's purpose by re-inserting human latency into every decomposition. The micro-debate's tentative lean toward review is overridden by the judge's verdict: its legitimate oversight concern is preserved more cheaply by atom_07 (operator-hold on retry exhaustion — review only the cases that actually fail) plus atom_11 (PROJECT-channel regression coverage), and by the fact that the PARENT was already operator-approved. Note: the contract's known_context still calls for the design+atom list to be reviewed before IMPLEMENTATION — that one-time design review is satisfied by this very document being submitted for operator sign-off, which is distinct from a per-decomposition runtime gate on every child.

open_questions: Concrete thresholds for the atom_01 scope profile: what acceptance_count / subsystem_count / estimated_turns values flip 'large'? Needs calibration against historical bridge-self tasks (the 29/30 timed-out workers are a labeled dataset).
Source of intent.estimated_turns when an intent does not provide it — derive from acceptance_count/subsystem_count, or treat absence as a neutral signal?
atom_09 dual-marker redundancy: keep both [[PROJECT_BACKLOG]] JSON and [[DECOMPOSED:N]], or derive N from the JSON length to avoid drift? (JSON should be source of truth.)
Exact retry cap for atom_07: 2 or 3 attempts, and does each retry re-run the full planner turn or only the decomposition sub-step?
Does an operator-hold surfacing/notification path already exist, or must one be built so held parents (atom_07) are not silently stuck?
Does Add-ProjectBacklogFromMarker's return object already expose per-atom single-file/acceptance validation (atom_06), or must per-atom checks be added to it?
Subsystem_count derivation: how is 'subsystem' counted deterministically (touched lib/* modules, declared in planner output, or inferred)?
implementation_plan: Phase 0 (guardrails first): Implement atom_05 channel fence (main/bridge only) and atom_08 consolidation contract (one largeness fn, one ingest path, one gate site) as the structural frame; add atom_11 PROJECT-channel regression tests up front so every later change runs against the non-interference invariant.

Phase 1 (classifier): Implement atom_01 — replace Test-IsLargeTask body (lib/prompt-builder.ps1:538-551) with the scope profile (acceptance_count, subsystem_count, intent.estimated_turns), keeping the atom/decomposed-child early-return. Land threshold defaults as constants pending calibration (open question).

Phase 2 (planner contract): Implement atom_09 — update the planner prompt for large bridge-self parents to emit [[PROJECT_BACKLOG]] JSON (single-file atoms with acceptance/checks + parent linkage) plus [[DECOMPOSED:N]].

Phase 3 (ingest + validation): Implement atom_02 — route the marker through Add-ProjectBacklogFromMarker(Channel='main', SourceTaskId=parent) (lib/backlog-autopilot.ps1:1383); implement atom_06 — define valid split from the ingest return (created>=2, errors empty, single-file + acceptance + linkage per atom), extending the return object with per-atom validation if needed.

Phase 4 (children): Implement atom_04 (modified) — create children status='approved', tag bridge-self, link via source_task_id; redirect/deprecate the Add-Idea(status='new') child path (lib/backlog-crud.ps1:74-89) for the bridge-self atom case only.

Phase 5 (mandatory gate + retry): Implement atom_03 — block STATUS: CONTINUE to the coder when a large bridge-self parent has no valid split; implement atom_07 — bounded decompose-retry (2-3) feeding deterministic ingest errors back into the prompt, terminal operator-hold on exhaustion, never code-the-monolith.

Phase 6 (verification): Extend atom_11 tests to cover the full path: large main task auto-splits into approved single-file atoms that commit < 15 min; large main task with invalid split blocks the coder and retries then holds; large PROJECT task still requires F1-F4 and does not auto-split.
Operator gate: Submit THIS MAP/PLAN + atom list for one-time operator sign-off before any implementation (design-only deliverable per the contract).
next_step: Submit this MAP/PLAN and the accepted atom list (atom_01, atom_02, atom_03, atom_04-modified, atom_05, atom_06, atom_07, atom_08, atom_09, atom_11) for one-time operator review; on approval, begin Phase 0 by landing the atom_05 channel fence plus atom_11 PROJECT-channel regression tests as the guardrail frame before touching Test-IsLargeTask.

red_team_findings.what: atom_04's core claim — approved children 'bypass subsequent control-plane gates' — is factually false against the live code. Test-BacklogApprovedItemClaimable returns claimable=false / reason='control-plane-blocked' for an APPROVED bridge-self atom touching a control-plane file unless it carries a valid bridge_self_admission canary record (lib/backlog.ps1:445-522; regression tools/test-autopilot-controlplane-gate.ps1:41-50). Approval does NOT bypass this gate. The design never mentions bridge_self_admission anywhere.
red_team_findings.why: bridge-self self-improvement atoms touch lib/*.ps1 and driver.ps1 BY DEFINITION (the bridge editing its own control plane). So the majority of decomposed atoms will be created 'approved', pass atom_06 validation, be judged a 'valid split', and then be blocked at claim time and never coded. This directly fails success_test #3 (atoms bypass control-plane gates) and success_test #7 (<15 min commit) for exactly the class of tasks the feature targets — re-creating the 'children re-stick on control-plane gates' problem the design claims to eliminate.

red_team_findings.what: Creating children directly as status='approved' (atom_04) bypasses Invoke-BacklogHeldItemAutoTriage — the EXISTING mechanism that attaches bridge_self_admission to control-plane items. That triage only processes 'new'/'held' items (tools/test-held-item-auto-triage.ps1:38,51-52 shows it flips a 'new' CP item to 'approved' WHILE attaching the canary admission). By short-circuiting straight to 'approved', the design strips the admission-granting step.
red_team_findings.why: Result: approved-but-unadmitted control-plane atoms that are permanently control-plane-blocked at claim. The very path atom_08/step-5 wants to 'deprecate/redirect' (status='new' → triage) is the path that grants admission. Removing it without replacing the admission attachment makes the atoms unclaimable — a self-inflicted deadlock the design did not detect because it misdiagnosed the 'new' status as purely a re-approval nuisance.

red_team_findings.what: Unresolved admission dilemma. To be claimable, a control-plane atom needs a valid bridge_self_admission with admitted=true, canary_required=true, checks matching driver -SelfTest / smoke / canary, and a rollback_plan (lib/backlog.ps1:454-485). Either (a) the planner auto-emits this per atom — meaning the autopilot self-grants control-plane admission for its own changes, rubber-stamping and defeating the bridge_self_admission safety gate the recent commits just added — or (b) it doesn't, and atoms are blocked. The design picks neither; atom_09's schema lists only slug/title/task/files/acceptance/checks/risk.
red_team_findings.why: Option (a) violates the spirit of the constraints (anti-frankenstein / 'no conflicting gates') for the MOST sensitive channel by turning a real safety gate into a no-op auto-approve. Option (b) is the availability deadlock above. The design's claim of satisfying both automation and oversight collapses precisely at the control-plane boundary, which is where bridge-self work lives.

red_team_findings.what: Retry × dedup interaction strands valid splits. Add-ProjectBacklogFromMarker skips already-existing slugs (lib/backlog-autopilot.ps1:1412 → $skipped++, NOT an error) and returns created excluding skips (line 1465). atom_06 defines a valid split as created>=2 with errors empty, measured from one ingest call. atom_07 retries on invalid.
red_team_findings.why: After a partial first attempt creates some atoms, a decompose-retry re-emitting the full split sees the earlier atoms as duplicate slugs → skipped (not created, not errors). created drops below 2 with errors empty → atom_06 declares the split invalid → retries exhaust → parent goes to operator-hold even though a complete, valid split already exists in the backlog. Breaks success_test #6's intent and permanently strands good decompositions.

red_team_findings.what: atom_06 ('each atom = exactly one target file, derived from the ingest return value') is not implementable as written. The reused validator Test-ProjectAutopilotTaskMetadata only requires files.Count>=1 and explicitly allows multiple files (lib/backlog-autopilot.ps1:1287, 1420 takes First 12). The ingest return value (created/skipped/errors/ids/slugs/chapters, line 1465) carries no per-atom file count.
red_team_findings.why: The one-file property cannot be checked from the return value without re-reading each created item — contradicting atom_06's own 'from the ingest return value, not by re-scanning' framing. The only alternative is modifying the shared Test-ProjectAutopilotTaskMetadata to enforce one-file, which would reject legitimate multi-file PROJECT atoms and regress the PROJECT path — colliding with atom_05/atom_11's non-interference guarantee.

red_team_findings.what: The atomicity criterion ('1 file AND passes ParseFile/smoke by itself') is frequently unsatisfiable for real feature decomposition. Coupled changes (caller+callee, function+its test, signature change + call sites) cannot be both single-file and independently green: a caller-before-callee atom won't pass smoke alone.
red_team_findings.why: The planner is forced to choose between multi-file atoms (violating one-file) or atoms that fail smoke in isolation (violating verifiability) → chronic atom_06 validation failures → repeated decompose-retry → operator-hold. The goal's atomicity definition over-constrains, and the design provides no dependency-ordering / staged-commit story (the ingest captures depends_on at line 1421 but the design never uses it), so the 'each atom green by itself' success metric is unreachable for genuinely coupled work.

red_team_findings.what: Test-IsLargeTask's scope inputs are non-deterministic and/or unavailable at classification time. intent.estimated_turns is an LLM estimate (contradicting atom_01's stated rejection of an 'LLM-judge … non-deterministic' approach), and acceptance_count / subsystem_count are absent on a short raw idea ('build service X') before any planning pass populates them.
red_team_findings.why: The exact success_test #5 case (short text, wide scope) can still score zero on acceptance/subsystem counts and be classified small, slipping through — the same failure as the char/regex heuristic it replaces. Deriving subsystem_count deterministically without regressing to file-count is flagged as an open question, yet success_test #5 depends on solving it. The classifier is only as deterministic as inputs that are themselves model-generated or empty.

red_team_findings.what: operator-hold (atom_07's terminal state) is not durable. Invoke-BacklogHeldItemAutoTriage is a driver maintenance job that auto-promotes 'held'/'new' items back to 'approved' (tools/test-held-item-auto-triage.ps1:50-55: narrow-CP held item → approved+admission; only BROAD multi-CP-file items stay held).
red_team_findings.why: A large parent sent to 'held' on retry exhaustion can be auto-re-approved by triage. Since the parent is untagged, it re-classifies as large and either re-enters the decompose loop (ping-pong) or, if triage admits/approves it, advances toward a coder as the monolith — leaking through the 'never code the monolith' invariant (atom_03) via an existing automated path the design didn't account for.

red_team_findings.what: The decompose turn is itself output-cap-prone — a recursion of the failure it fixes. Each atom must carry slug/title/task(body ≥40 chars, line 1416)/files/acceptance/checks/risk (Test-ProjectAutopilotTaskMetadata) — plus a full canary admission for control-plane atoms — or it is skipped.
red_team_findings.why: A high-fidelity N-atom spec for a genuinely large task is itself a large single-turn generation. The same output-cap that kills 45-minute coder turns can truncate the planner's decompose turn → partial/invalid split → retry/hold. The design assumes decomposition is cheap and atomic, but for the biggest tasks (the ones that matter) it inherits the same single-turn budget ceiling.

red_team_findings.what: atom_10's operator-review reconciliation is internally inconsistent. It claims the operator inspects the MAP/PLAN at the EXISTING parent-approval point 'before decomposition runs' — but the MAP/PLAN and atom list are produced BY the planner DURING decomposition; they do not exist at parent-approval time.
red_team_findings.why: Reviewing the actual atoms requires a post-planning / pre-dispatch checkpoint, which is a new gate — the very thing atom_08 forbids and the rejected original atom_10 proposed. As designed, the operator approves only the raw parent intent and never sees the generated atoms before they auto-dispatch (the async atom review is 'optional'). The design's claim to preserve operator visibility is therefore not actually met for the atoms themselves.

red_team_findings.what: The decision's own atom list violates the atomicity contract it mandates. Multiple atoms target the same file (atom_02/03/06/07 → lib/backlog-autopilot.ps1; atom_01/09 → lib/prompt-builder.ps1; atom_04/08 → lib/backlog-crud.ps1) and implementation_plan orders them with hard dependencies (atom_03 needs atom_06+atom_07; atom_04 needs atom_06).
red_team_findings.why: Applied to this design's own output, success_test #2 ('each atom targets a single file and represents a small, independently-verifiable change') fails: the atoms are neither single-file nor independently committable (e.g., landing atom_03's coder-blocking gate without atom_06's validator and atom_07's retry bound yields a broken/spinning gate). The design does not eat its own dog food, which suggests the one-file atomicity rule it imposes on the planner is impractical even for its authors.

red_team_findings.what: atom_04's stated known-context premise is partly wrong. Children created via the chosen path (Add-ProjectBacklogFromMarker, lib/backlog-autopilot.ps1:1449) are ALREADY status='approved', tagged 'bridge-self'/'atom', and source-linked. The status='new' re-stick problem (backlog-crud.ps1:74-89) is the RAW Add-Idea path, which this design does not use.
red_team_findings.why: atom_08/step-5's 'deprecate/redirect the Add-Idea(status=new) child path' fixes a path the chosen design never invokes, while the real blocker (missing bridge_self_admission on approved CP atoms) is left unaddressed. Misdiagnosis steers implementation effort at a non-problem and gives false confidence that the re-stick is solved.
